Donation Policy

All donations are received subject to our site privacy policy below. All donations over $2 to approved aid and development projects are tax deductible in Australia (and in the USA and (over $5) New Zealand).

The Australian Tax Office (ATO) requires: 1. If funds raised exceed the requirement for any project, the funds may be directed to another project, 2. Tax deductible donations are required to be unconditional gifts and accordingly OneTomorrow Charitable Fund, Global Development Group or Australian Communities Foundation cannot always guarantee that a donor’s preference will be granted.

Please note that no non-development activities (evangelism, welfare or political activities) are funded by, or are a part of OneTomorrow aid and development projects. If, in their own time, OneTomorrow staff, committee, volunteers and contractors of partner organisations undertake or participate in evangelism, proselytism and missionary work, partisan political activities or welfare, they must ensure that their activities are not perceived or viewed as being on behalf of or representative of OneTomorrow Charitable Fund.
To administer and collect donations OneTomorrow works with two giving partners.
Australian Communities Foundation

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is a sub-fund of Australian Communities Foundation (ACF).  ACF provide administrative paperwork, due diligence and compliance by managing OneTomorrow’s funds and providing giving guidance for charitable causes.  Depending on the cause you select your donation may be processed directly by ACF and be matched from the One Tomorrow Charitable Fund.  ACF will collect identity and contact data regarding your donation and will share that with OneTomorrow Charitable Fund.  You may view the ACF Privacy Policy here.
https://www.communityfoundation.org.au/policies/privacy
Global Development Group

Global Development Group is an Australian, non-government, humanitarian development organisation working with approved partners to relieve poverty and provide long-term solutions through quality aid and development projects.  Global Development Group works together with ACFID and DFAT to ensure that the highest accountability standards are met.  One Tomorrow Charitable Fund is an Australian based fund-raising partner of GDG.  Depending on the cause you select your donation may go direct to GDG and be matched by the One Tomorrow Charitable Fund.  GDG will collect identity and contact data regarding your donation and will share that with One Tomorrow Charitable Fund.  You may view the GDG Privacy Policy here:
https://globaldevelopmentgroup.org/au/help/site-user-policy/
Privacy Policy

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is a charitable brand of APT Travel Group (ATG).
ATG takes the privacy of your personal information very seriously. Find out what information OneTomorrow (APT) collects about you, and how it may be used.
Last updated 4 November, 2021.
MANAGEMENT OF PERSONAL INFORMATION

At APT, we recognise the importance of your privacy and understand your concerns about the security of the personal information you provide to us.  This privacy policy explains how we use any personal information we collect about you, and your rights to access and correct the personal information we hold about you.

In this policy, APT means the entities within the APT Travel Group, including Australian Pacific Touring Pty Ltd, Australian Pacific (Holdings) Pty Ltd, and their subsidiaries and related entities which operate the APT, Travelmarvel, TravelGlo, Botanica World Discoveries, Captain’s Choice and OneTomorrow brands.  APT is the controller responsible for your personal data (collectively referred to “we”, “us” or “our” in this Privacy Policy).

We comply with the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) as contained in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).  Along with other regional regulations like the GDPR, the APPs detail how personal information may be collected, used, disclosed, stored and destroyed, and how an individual may gain access to or make complaints about the personal information held about them.

There are different kinds of data, below are some examples:
•
Identity Data

includes first name, last name, date of birth and gender.
•
Contact Data

includes address, email address and telephone numbers.
•
Financial Data

includes bank account and payment card details.
•
Technical Data

includes IP address, your login data, and your browser type.
•
Profile Data
includes your username and password and survey responses.

We may collect anonymised details about your use of the websites for the purposes of aggregate statistics or reporting purposes. Aggregated data (your data combined with other people’s data) may come from your personal data but if it does not directly or indirectly reveal your identity, it is not considered personal data. For example, we may combine and analyse your use of the website to work out the number of users accessing a specific website feature.
Personal information

is information or an opinion about an identified individual, or about an individual who is reasonably identifiable.  We collect personal information from and about our prospective and current customers, as well as from and about travel agents, business partners and other travel suppliers.
Sensitive Information

, a sub-set of personal information, includes information or an opinion about an individual’s racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, political association membership, religious beliefs or affiliations, philosophical beliefs, professional or trade association membership, trade union membership, sexual orientation or practices or criminal record, as well as health, genetic and biometric information.  We collect sensitive information from and about our customers where such information is included in Government-issued identity documents (e.g. passport), and from health and mobility questionnaires.
Health Information

is information or an opinion about an individual’s health or disability, the health services provided or to be provided to them, their expressed wishes for the provision of future health services, personal information collected to provide a health service, personal information collected in connection with organ and body-part donation, and predictive genetic information.

This policy details how APT manages personal information about you (including sensitive information and health information), whether you are a customer, a travel agent, an employee or another kind of travel supplier to our business.

In the course of offering our travel products and services, the collection of personal information is necessary and unavoidable.  However, we aim to only collect personal information that is reasonable and fair in order to deliver the best possible travel products and services.

We take our obligations very seriously and have appointed a Privacy Officer for Australia, New Zealand and North America and a Data Protection Officer for Europe and the United Kingdom (together and separately (as applicable) the “DPO”) who are responsible for overseeing questions or concerns you may have about this Privacy Policy, including any requests to exercise your legal rights.  The APT contact details are shown at the end of this policy.
It is important that the personal data we hold about you is accurate and current. Please keep us informed if your personal data changes during your relationship with us.
WHAT PERSONAL INFORMATION WE COLLECT AND HOLD

The kinds of personal information we collect from you or about you depend on the transaction you have entered into with us, the travel products / services you or your organisation have contracted us to provide, and the travel products / services you or your organisation are interested in.

If you are a customer, the kinds of personal information and sensitive information that we commonly collect and hold from you or about you include:  your name, address, phone, fax and mobile numbers, email address, date of birth, nationality, religion, drivers licence details, passport details (including number, nationality, issue date, expiry date), bank account details, travel preferences and experiences, travel insurance and travel rewards and loyalty program membership.  We also collect health information relating to your current and previous health status, current and previous medical conditions, and your religious, cultural and dietary requirements.  We also collect personal information, sensitive information and health information from or about your family members, next of kin, emergency contact details and/or other members of your travelling party.

If you are an employee or contractor of APT (or a prospective employee or contractor), the kinds of personal information that we commonly collect and hold from you or about you may include:  your name, address, gender, date of birth, telephone numbers, voice and image, email address, education, qualifications and employment experience, proof of citizenship or passport details to verify proof of ability to work in the designated country, CV or resume, statements addressing the criteria, background checks, referee checks, notes recorded during the application process, banking, tax and superannuation accounts and identification numbers, next of kin or emergency contact details, and medical certificates or health information you supply. We generally collect personal information directly from you, but may also collect personal information from other sources (e.g. recruitment agents).

We record anonymous clickstream information from every visitor to our website.  We use this information to ensure that our website remains relevant and appropriate for the majority of users.  We do not make any association between this information and your personal details.  For further information, please see our Cookies Policy.

When you browse our website, contact us electronically, or engage with us on social media, we may also record: geographical tagging, cookies, your IP address and statistical data from your activity. When engaging with us on social media channels, your data may also be collected and used for the purpose of targeted advertising.

By using our Digital Channels, you agree to our privacy and cookie policies and consent to the use of cookies and similar technologies by us and our carefully selected third party partners as described in these policies. 
Credit card details are processed via a secure and Payment Card Industry compliant payment gateway and not stored on APT’s servers when you book, or pay for travel products through our website or contact centre systems.  If you would like more details on how we process credit card payments please send a request to the contact details given at the end of this document.
HOW WE COLLECT AND HOLD PERSONAL INFORMATION

We aim to collect personal information only directly from you, unless it is unreasonable or impracticable for us to do so.  For example, if you are a customer of APT, we collect personal information from you or about you from your letters, emails, and telephone calls with us, and from your activity and inputs on our website and social media platforms.  We also collect personal information from you or about you from booking forms, application forms, customer satisfaction and post-trip surveys, requests you submit in person or through our website for a brochure, and other documents that you submit to or through us.  We may collect personal information about you as submitted by your family members and/or other members of your travelling party.

However, in many instances we may also receive personal information about you, your family members and/or other members of your travelling party as submitted by third parties, such as your travel agent/s who are making the travel arrangements for you, travel insurers, airlines, hotel partners, tour operators and providers and affiliated travel suppliers.

You can be anonymous or use a pseudonym when dealing with us, unless:
•	the use of your true identity is a legal requirement (eg. booking travel arrangements); or
•	it is impracticable for us to deal with you on such basis.

Personal information may be collected by us and by our third party service providers who assist us in operating the website. Including:
1.	Google Analytics:
 We use Google Analytics to help analyse how you use our website. Google Analytics generates statistical and other information about website use by means of cookies. Google will store this information.
If you do not want your website visit information reported by Google Analytics, you can install the Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on. For more details on installing and uninstalling the add-on, please visit the Google Analytics opt-out page at https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout.

2.	Click Stream Information
In common with many websites, when you read, browse or download information from our website, we or our internet service provider may also collect information such as the date and time of your visit to the Website, the pages accessed and any information downloaded. This information is used for statistical, reporting and website administration, maintenance and improvement purposes only.
If you are an employee or contractor of APT, we collect personal information from you or about you for the purposes related to your employment or engagement.
Raisely

This website uses the Raisely Platform. Raisely collects identity and contact data to create a data base for us to contact you. It facilitates the transmission financial data to Australian Communities Foundation or Global Development Group to facilitate your donation. It records which cause you donate to and provides OneTomorrow with consolidated data with which to match your donation.
Australian Communities Foundation

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is a sub-fund of Australian Communities Foundation (ACF). ACF provide administrative paperwork, due diligence and compliance by managing OneTomorrow’s funds and providing giving guidance for charitable causes. Depending on the cause you select your donation may go direct to ACF and be matched from the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund. ACF will collect identity and contact data regarding your donation and will share that with OneTomorrow Charitable Fund.
Global Development Group

Global Development Group is an Australian, non-government, humanitarian development organisation working with approved partners to relieve poverty and provide long-term solutions through quality aid and development projects. Global Development Group works together with ACFID and DFAT to ensure that the highest accountability standards are met. OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is an Australian based fund-raising partner of GDG. Depending on the cause you select, your donation may go direct to GDG and be matched by the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund. GDG will collect identity and contact data regarding your donation and will share that with OneTomorrow Charitable Fund.  This data is transmitted to ATG via password protected Google Forms with limited access to approved OneTomorrow and ATG employees.  ATG stores your information in a secured digital file format and in Salesforce.  You can learn more about Salesforce security here.
https://trust.salesforce.com/en/security/for-administrators/
USING YOUR PERSONAL DATA
We will only use your personal data when the law allows us to. Most commonly, we will use your personal data in the following circumstances:
•	Where we need to perform the contract we are about to enter into or have entered into with you.
•	Where it is necessary for our legitimate interests (or those of a third party) and your interests and fundamental rights do not override those interests.
•	Where we need to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation.

We have set out below, in a table format, a description of all the ways we plan to use your personal data, and which of the legal bases we rely on to do so. We have also identified what our legitimate interests are where appropriate.

Note that we may process your personal data using more than one lawful ground depending on the specific purpose for which we are using your data. Please refer to our contact details at the bottom of this policy if you need details about the specific legal ground we are relying on to process your personal data where more than one ground has been set out in the table below.

leaves.text: Change of purpose:

We will only use your personal data for the purposes for which we collected it, unless we reasonably consider that we need to use it for another reason and that reason is compatible with or reasonably related to the original purpose. If we need to use your personal data for an unrelated purpose, we will notify you and we will explain the legal basis which allows us to do so.
Please note that we may process your personal data without your knowledge or consent, in compliance with the above rules, where this is required or permitted by law.
WHY WE COLLECT, HOLD, USE AND DISCLOSE PERSONAL INFORMATION

We collect, hold, use and disclose personal information from you or about you where it is reasonably necessary for us to carry out our business functions and activities (please see the table above for further details).
We do not disclose your personal information without your permission, unless the disclosure is:
1.	In accordance with this Privacy Policy or any agreement you enter into with us;
2.	To our related companies;
3.	To third parties to whom we may choose to sell, transfer, or merge parts of our business or our assets; or
4.	Required or authorised by law.
We will routinely disclose some of your personal information to other Australian entities within the APT Group of travel companies in connection with the purposes set out in the table above.

Our business also necessarily works closely with external travel agents, travel suppliers, airlines, hotel partners, ground tour operators, caterers and travel insurers etc.  We routinely disclose your personal information to these third parties for them to assist us in carrying out our business functions and activities.  In some instances, these external businesses (especially travel agents) may have direct access to our CRM database for the purpose of providing streamlined booking and reservation services etc.

We require all third parties to respect the security of your personal information and to treat it in accordance with the law. We do not allow our third-party service providers to use your personal information for their own purposes and only permit them to process your personal information for specified purposes and in accordance with our instructions.

We may collect sensitive information from you or about you where there is a legal requirement to do so, or where we are otherwise permitted by law.  For example, we routinely collect and hold the details on your passport, such as your nationality.   Otherwise, we will specifically seek your consent to the collection, use and disclosure of sensitive information.  For example, we may seek to collect sensitive information about you where it is necessary or desirable for your travel experience.

If we do not collect, hold, use or disclose your personal information, or if you do not consent, then we may not be able to answer your enquiry, complete the transaction you have entered into, or provide the travel products and services that you or your organisation have contracted us to provide.

We also collect, hold, use and disclose your personal information for related purposes that you would reasonably expect, such as our administrative and accounting functions, identification checks, fraud checks, providing you with information about other travel products and services offered by us, sending you marketing communications and promotions via email or SMS, market research, customer feedback and quality assurance surveys, newsletter and magazine communications, statistical collation and website traffic analysis.  Some of these functions may be carried out directly by us, or through outsourcing to business partners such as mailing houses.
Where we wish to use or disclose your personal information for other purposes, we will obtain your consent.
MARKETING

Promotional offers from us: Where we use your personal information for marketing and promotional purposes, it is because you have asked to hear from APT, you have entered a competition and agreed to join our mailing list, or a friend / colleague has requested it on your behalf and you have confirmed this to us.
Third-party marketing: We will get your express opt-in consent before we share your personal data with any other company for marketing purposes.
Opting out: Opting out: You can opt out of our direct marketing efforts at any time by contacting
info@onetomorrow.com.au
or by notifying us. Opt out procedures are also included in our marketing communications.
We may also disclose your personal information to third parties (including government departments and enforcement bodies) where required or permitted by law.
CONTESTS

When you enter a contest or other promotional feature on our website, we may ask for your personal information so that we can administer the contest and notify winners. Participation in these contests is completely voluntary and you therefore have a choice whether or not to disclose the required information in order to participate.
ONLINE SURVEYS

We also value opinions and comments from our customers, and you may have the opportunity to give us your feedback through website and other surveys.  In conducting these surveys, we may ask for your personal information so that we can appropriately identify you.  Survey and personal information collected will be aggregated and used to make improvements to our website and to improve our products and services. Participation in these surveys is completely voluntary and you therefore have a choice whether or not to disclose the required information in order to participate.
HOW WE HOLD AND STORE PERSONAL INFORMATION
ATG and OneTomorrow Charitable Fund takes the security of any personal information we hold very seriously.

Your personal information is held and stored on paper and/or by electronic means, (including in Cloud-based systems).  We have physical, electronic and procedural safeguards in place for personal information and take reasonable steps to ensure that your personal information is protected from misuse, interference and loss, and from unauthorised access, modification and disclosure:
•	Data held and stored on paper is stored in lockable filing cabinets, within secure premises, with secured entry and monitored alarms.

•	Data held and stored electronically (including in the Cloud) is protected by internal and external firewalls, limited access via file passwords, and files can be designated read-only or no access.  We also require our IT contractors and other third parties to implement privacy safeguards.
•	Data stored or archived off-site is contained within secure facilities.  We also require our storage contractors to implement privacy safeguards.

•	Where we disclose personal information to third parties (including contractors and affiliated businesses located locally and overseas), our contractual arrangements with them include specific privacy requirements.
•	Our staff receive regular training on privacy procedures.

In addition, we limit access to your personal data to those employees, agents, contractors and other third parties who have a business need to know. They will only process your personal data on our instructions and they are subject to a duty of confidentiality.

While we take great care to protect your personal information in all of our business systems, unfortunately no information transmission over the Internet can be guaranteed to be 100% secure. Accordingly, we cannot ensure or warrant the security of any information you send to us or receive from us online. This is particularly true for information you send to us via email. We have no way of protecting that information until it reaches us.
DESTRUCTION AND DE-IDENTIFICATION
We will retain your personal information whilst it is required for any of our business functions, or for any other lawful purpose.
We use secure methods to destroy or to permanently de-identify your personal information when it is no longer needed:
•	Paper records are commonly shredded, pulped or disintegrated, or sent for secure destruction.
•	Electronic records are deleted from all locations, to the best of our ability, or encrypted and/or placed beyond use.
OVERSEAS DISCLOSURE

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund  is part of the international APT Group of companies.  We will routinely disclose some of your personal information to overseas entities within the APT Group.  Our related entities are located in Germany, New Zealand, the UK, Canada and the USA.
APT contact details are shown at the end of this policy if you want further information about the specific mechanisms we use when transferring your personal data outside of the EEA.

Our business is also necessarily affiliated with a range of third party businesses and travel suppliers located overseas.  In the course of doing business with you, we will routinely disclose some of your personal information (including sensitive information and health information) to these overseas recipients, but only when we can ensure an adequate level of protection.  Our third party overseas affiliates are located in our APT Destinations, including Africa, Asia, Canada, Alaska, the USA, Egypt, Jordan, Europe, New Zealand, Russia, Scandinavia, the Baltics, South America and the South Pacific.

We will only disclose your personal information to overseas recipients where it is necessary to complete the transaction you have entered into, and:
•	you have provided consent; or
•	we believe on reasonable grounds that the overseas recipient is required to deal with your personal information by enforceable laws which are similar to the requirements under the APPs; or
•	it is otherwise permitted by law.
LEGAL RIGHTS UNDER THE GDPR
Under certain circumstances, the GDPR grants you certain rights under information protection laws in relation to your personal information. You have the right to:

1.	Request access to your personal information (commonly known as a “data subject access request”). This enables you to receive a copy of the personal information we hold about you and to check that we are lawfully processing it.

2.	Request correction of the personal information that we hold about you. This enables you to have any incomplete or inaccurate information we hold about you corrected, though we may need to verify the accuracy of the new information you provide to us.

3.	Request erasure of your personal information. This enables you to ask us to delete or remove personal information where there is no good reason for us continuing to process it. You also have the right to ask us to delete or remove your personal information where you have successfully exercised your right to object to processing (see below), where we may have processed your information unlawfully or where we are required to erase your personal information to comply with local law. Note, however, that we may not always be able to comply with your request of erasure for specific legal reasons which will be notified to you, if applicable, at the time of your request.

4.	Object to processing of your personal information where we are relying on a legitimate interest (or those of a third party) and there is something about your particular situation which makes you want to object to processing on this ground as you feel it impacts on your fundamental rights and freedoms. You also have the right to object where we are processing your personal information for direct marketing purposes. In some cases, we may demonstrate that we have compelling legitimate grounds to process your information which override your rights and freedoms.
5.	Request restriction of processing of your personal information. This enables you to ask us to suspend the processing of your personal information in the following scenarios:

6.	Request the transfer of your personal information to you or to a third party. We will provide to you, or a third party you have chosen, your personal information in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format. Note that this right only applies to automated information which you initially provided consent for us to use or where we used the information to perform a contract with you.
7.	Withdraw consent at any time where we are relying on consent to process your personal information. However, this will not affect the lawfulness of any processing carried out before you withdraw your consent. If you withdraw your consent, we may not be able to provide certain products or services to you. We will advise you if this is the case at the time you withdraw your consent.
If you wish to exercise any of the rights set out above, our contact details are shown at the end of this policy.
NO FEE USUALLY REQUIRED

You will not have to pay a fee to access your personal data (or to exercise any of the other rights). However, we may charge a reasonable fee if your request is clearly unfounded, repetitive or excessive. Alternatively, we may refuse to comply with your request in these circumstances.
WHAT WE MAY NEED FROM YOU

We may need to request specific information from you to help us confirm your identity and ensure your right to access your personal data (or to exercise any of your other rights). This is a security measure to ensure that personal data is not disclosed to any person who has no right to receive it. We may also contact you to ask you for further information in relation to your request to speed up our response.
TIME LIMIT TO RESPOND

We try to respond to all legitimate requests within one month. Occasionally it may take us longer than a month if your request is particularly complex or you have made a number of requests. In this case, we will notify you and keep you updated.
REQUESTS FOR ACCESS AND CORRECTION
We have procedures in place for dealing with and responding to requests for access to, and correction of, the personal information held about you.

In most cases, we expect that we will be able to comply with your request.  However, if we do not agree to provide you access or to correct the information as requested, we will give you written reasons why.  Please contact us using the regional guidelines listed below for further information.
To assist us to keep our records up-to-date, please notify us of any changes to your personal information.
COMPLAINTS AND CONCERNS
For Residents of Australia

We have procedures in place for dealing with complaints and concerns about our practices in relation to the Privacy Act and the Australian Privacy Principles.  We will respond to your complaint in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Australian Privacy Principles.  Please use our Australian contact address below for further information.

It is also important that you contact us immediately in the unlikely event that you have reason to believe that your privacy has been breached. In turn, we undertake to inform you as soon as possible in the unlikely event that we have cause to believe that your privacy information may have been breached by any error in our systems. We have put in place procedures to deal with any suspected personal data breach and will notify you and any applicable regulator of a breach where we are legally required to do so.

While you have the right to make a complaint at any time to the Office of the Australian Information Commission (OAIC), we will appreciate the opportunity to address your concerns first. As such, we shall be grateful if you will contact us before approaching the Office of the Australian Information Commission (OAIC).
For Residents of EU & EEA countries including the United Kingdom

Where your data controller is an APT Group company located in the UK or another EU or EEA Member State, you have the right to make a complaint at any time to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), the UK supervisory authority for data protection issues (www.ico.org.uk) or any other applicable EU national supervisory authority. However, we will appreciate the opportunity to address your concerns first. As such, we shall be grateful if you will contact us before approaching the ICO.
For Residents of other countries

Please contact our Australian office at the address below with regard to any complaints or concerns you have with regard our Privacy Policy. Where we are obliged to follow privacy laws in the country of purchase we shall do so. To the extent permissible, the principles which apply in Australia will apply.
LINKS

The OneTomorrow Charitable Fund website may contain links to other websites. Please note that when you click on one of these links, you are entering another website. APT encourage you to read the privacy statements of these linked sites as their privacy policy may differ from ours.

Responsible Travel
What is Responsible Travel?

The world is waking up to the need for more sustainable ways of travelling, and here at OneTomorrow we understand we have a responsibility to our planet. Responsible travel is all about being socially and culturally aware, minimising our environmental footprint and travelling in a way that takes into consideration the locals, environment and individual cultures. We encourage this sustainable way of travel through journeys with the APT Travel Group (ATG).

The UN defines the responsible traveller as one who keeps an open mind towards new cultures and traditions. They respect human rights. They participate in activities which safeguard natural environments. And responsible travellers will buy local goods to contribute to social and economic development.
Our Guiding Principles
Our vision of conscientious travel involves protecting the environment, respecting local communities and ensuring the wellbeing of the individuals within those communities.
As part of our commitment to achieving this, we have embraced the
UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

. The SDGs address the global challenges we face, and present a set plan to achieve a fair and sustainable future for everyone. In order to make a more powerful impact, we will begin by focussing on the three SDGs listed below. Our ultimate vision is to incorporate more goals with time in order to attain our shared aspiration for a better future.
Good Health and Wellbeing
Improving access to essential health services; addressing the burden of non-communicable diseases, including mental health; and stepping up the fight against antimicrobial resistance.
Quality Education

Increasing proficiency in reading and mathematics; ensuring quality of education keeps pace with technological advancement; and improving learning outcomes, particularly for women, girls and marginalised individuals.
Life on the Land
Halt and reverse land degradation; preserve and restore biodiversity; and protect endangered species from the threat of extinction.
Our Responsible Travel Commitments

The APT Travel Group (ATG) cares about giving its guests unforgettable journeys – ones that benefit everyone involved. Here at OneTomorrow, we endorse various initiatives across the company, working together so you can travel with the assurance that the places you visit are impacted positively. Below is a snapshot of the various initiatives we are running.
Supporting Indigenous Communities in the Kimberley

An Advanced Ecotourism certificate in the Kimberley speaks volumes about the commitment APT Travel Group (ATG) and OneTomorrow have to maintain our long-standing Indigenous partnerships in Australia. Some of our areas of work include creating sustainable employment opportunities and making donations to the local communities.
Reducing Plastic Waste on Tour

For each minute of every single day, the equivalent of a truckload of plastic enters our world’s waterways. The APT Travel Group (ATG) is committed to changing this. From July 2019, all single-use plastic bottles have been removed on APT and Travelmarvel Mekong and Irrawaddy river cruises. Brand-new Travelmarvel ships on Europe’s waterways are now fitted with environmental water stations. And on our APT Small Ships, refillable water bottles are provided to all guests. Each day, we continue to work with our suppliers in the effort to eliminate single-use plastic bottles in other areas on tour.
Respecting Local Cultures

Throughout journeys with APT Travel Group (ATG), we place a heavy importance on respecting the rights, history, culture and dignity of local and Indigenous people, wherever we go. Encountering local cultures is often the highlight of travelling the world, and it’s important as visitors that we honour them.
Plant-a-Tree Scheme

We’ve reduced the amount of paper used company-wide, choosing to go digital wherever possible. We envision a future where guests on tour with APT Travel Group (ATG) will be able to opt to receive their travel documents electronically. When you choose to go paper-free, OneTomorrow will plant a tree in bushfire-stricken communities. This way, we can help support a more sustainable future.
OneTomorrow Charitable Fund

By forming OneTomorrow, APT Travel Group (ATG) are taking the necessary steps towards responsible travel, continually finding ways to move closer to the ultimate goal of sustainability. Through guest and workplace giving programs, and a range of fundraising efforts, we are collectively working to help people and places around the world.

Antarctica

The Antarctic Science Foundation’s ultimate mission is to protect our planet. This Australian-based charity funds critical research to understand and protect Antarctica in order to help the world prepare and adapt to climate change, now and for generations to come.
The Problem

Antarctica is experiencing major warming due to climate change. This wild continent feels the effects of climate change faster than the rest of the planet, and Antarctica’s wildlife – including penguins, whales and seals – are particularly vulnerable to this. Climate science undertaken in Antarctica is the key to understanding our global climate future.
The Solution

Regular donations ensure funding of critical research into climate change and Antarctica’s wildlife and oceans. With the development of innovative technology and working with some of the world’s top Antarctic scientists, Antarctic Science Foundation can continue their work protecting wildlife and making accurate predictions of global climate.

causes.name: Thin Green Line
causes.description:
Rangers are the missing link in conservation. That’s why I’ll do everything I can to support The Thin Green Line Foundation
— Dr Jane Goodall, DBE

public.richProfileDescription:
Worldwide


Thin Green Line is a global not-for-profit organisation that exists to support park and wildlife rangers in their fight for conservation.

Rangers play a key role in safeguarding the natural, cultural, and historical values of the world’s protected areas against threats such as the illegal wildlife trade, invasive species, and, increasingly, the adverse impacts of climate change. Yet, the role they play as the first line of defence against these threats remains poorly recognised and inadequately resourced.


The Problem

Today we are facing increasing challenges around the Globe: climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and pandemics with a high human and economic impact. These and many other problems are closely linked to a deteriorating environment generated by our unsustainable production and consumption patterns which heavily depend on nature and its services.


The Solution

Protected areas are one the most effective tools for the conservation of biodiversity. However, no protected area is manageable without Park Rangers. Rangers working in protected and conserved areas are responsible for managing large tracts of the planet’s lands and waters. They are often underutilized, underrecognized and underequipped. Men and women rangers around the planet are key to securing and improving management of all protected areas.


What difference will your money make?

$35 can provide an essential first aid kit.

$110 can provide a pair of sturdy waterproof walking boots.

$220 can provide a GPS unit to enable rangers to communicate and stay safe while working in remote areas in often challenging conditions.


 * Gifts to Thin Green Line in AUD, NZD and USD receive a Tax deductable receipt and are received subject to our donate/privacy policy.

causes.name: Terry Fox Foundation
causes.description: “I could not leave [the cancer ward] knowing these faces and feelings would still exist, even though I would be set free from mine. I was determined to take myself to the limit for this cause.” - Terry Fox

public.richProfileDescription:
Canada


This story is simple and powerful. Terry Fox lost his leg to osteogenic sarcoma at age 18, underwent 16 months of treatment and found he could not ignore the suffering he witnessed in the cancer wards. Terry decided to run across Canada to raise money for cancer research in a Marathon of Hope. He wasn’t doing the run to become famous; he wanted to create change and fund a cure for all cancers.


The Problem

Terry died on June 28, 1981 at the age 22. This bold and courageous Canadian was gone, but his legacy was just beginning. To date, over $900 million has been raised for cancer research in Terry’s name through the annual Terry Fox Run, held across Canada and around the world. Nearly 2 in 5 people in Canada will develop cancer during their lifetime and about 1 out of 4 Canadians are expected to die from cancer.


The Solution

Terry’s personal experience and research led him to a simple conclusion – more money was needed for cancer research. We support bold, innovative cancer research across Canada that helps lead to better diagnosis, treatment options and quality of life for those facing cancer. We invest your donations in the very best scientists in laboratories, clinics, and hospitals around the country.


What difference will your money make?

$100 will accelerate cancer research

$200 is an investment in the future that ensures we can continue to make progress in the fight against cancer for future generations.

$500 can support the Canadian Tissue Repository Network (CTRNet)

causes.name: Grizzly Bear Foundation
causes.description: Hope for grizzlies means hope for people. Now more than ever, we realize the importance of protecting planet earth to ensure the health and well-being of all living things, including ourselves. Protecting bears is one way we can effectively take action to restore our planet.

public.richProfileDescription:
Canada


In 2014 home builder, philanthropist and art collector Michael Audain, O.C., O.B.C., was visited by a grizzly bear and her two cubs in a dream. Curious, Michael travelled to the Great Bear Rainforest, where he lived a similar personal experience. Inspired, Michael returned to Vancouver to establish the Grizzly Bear Foundation.


The Problem

Prior to the Grizzly Bear Foundation the majestic Grizzly Bear had no voice in our communities, governments, and in the public’s hearts and minds. Sparked by the fight to end the hunting of grizzly bears in British Columbia, Michael’s vision to ensure a safe and healthy future for grizzly bears all across North America continues to fuel the Grizzly Bear Foundation’s important work many years later.


The Solution

We believe coexistence with grizzly bears is possible. As an organization, we work with communities, governments, and industry to achieve this goal. We support human-bear coexistence through research, outreach, and education by working collaboratively with the BC Conservation Officer Service, the Ministry of Agriculture, First Nations, partner organizations, and local communities.


To foster coexistence, we host public workshops, social activities, presentations, and webinars and produce informational brochures, podcasts and videos to further non-lethal coexistence tools and techniques.


What difference will your money make?

$300 will support our advocacy and policy reform projects to secure long-term protection.

$500 will support Indigenous leadership in long-term grizzly bear conservation.

$1000 will help reduce human-bear conflict and promote coexistence.


 * OneTomorrow Charitable Fund matches donations up to $200,000 per year and up to $1,000 per individual donor. 

* Gifts to the Grizzly Foundation do not receive a Tax deductable receipt and are received subject to our donate/privacy policy.

causes.description: Severe storms in the Pacific are only getting worse, but through your donations we can reduce their impact.

public.richProfileDescription:
New Zealand

Habitat for Humanity holds the fundamental belief that everyone deserves a decent place to live. Habitat for Humanity’s housing initiatives and advocacy efforts in Aotearoa New Zealand and the Pacific are all designed to build pathways that lead towards an adequate home, whatever that may mean for a person or family’s personal journey, culture or circumstance. From supplying curtains to facilitating home ownership, Habitat’s many pathways are formed on the pillars of education, adequacy and stability through safe shelter.

The Problem

When the next weather event occurs, communities are better prepared with strengthened housing and the skills to recover quickly if needed.

At the same time, they are ensuring their efforts support the Traditional Land Owners of the Kuku Yalanji people. By buying properties currently residing in the Daintree Lowland Rainforest, the protected Daintree National Park and Wet Tropics World Heritage Area will regain its lost land. The Problem

Antarctica and the Southern Ocean are the global engine room of Earth’s climate, profoundly influencing weather systems through its oceans and atmosphere. At twice the size of Australia, this wild, pristine continent is now humanity’s “canary in the coal mine” and the focus of considerable change. Our challenge is to shape our future by listening and discovering what we need to know in the present.

The Solution

When you support the Antarctic Science Foundation, you will be backing dedicated, tenacious researchers to be curious as they confront uncertainty in the most extreme conditions. You will support these scientists to ask the important questions to sustain our way of life through tangible outcomes in:

  • Climate prediction for all Australians, living in our cities and those who live on the land
  • Fire, flood and drought prediction and mitigation
  • Managing economic and sustainable fisheries
  • Carbon capture and abatement via nature’s systems

posts.title: Leading Change: Collaborating for a better future in Vietnam
posts.body:
Who are the Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation?

There is a good chance that you haven’t heard of Blue Dragon yet, but since their small beginnings in 2003, Blue Dragon has become a powerful force for change on the streets of Vietnam, both in bustling cities and in rural areas where poverty is widespread. A huge percentage of Vietnamese children are born into poverty; rice farming is a major industry and sadly it is not unusual for whole families to earn $1 - $2 a day. Due to these difficult conditions, children often have to leave school and move out of their homes, making them vulnerable to homelessness, sexual exploitation and human trafficking.

Blue Dragon offers a holistic range of services to address the issues created by poverty in Vietnam, including shelter, legal advocacy, and long-term support to return to school and training. Blue Dragon also works tirelessly to find and rescue children from the trafficking trade, sometimes having to travel to countries across Asia to bring the children safely back to Vietnam.

Help from OneTomorrow

OneTomorrow is a charitable fund established by the APT Travel Group in 2019, to help create a positive, enduring impact on the nature and communities we touch in our travels across the globe. OneTomorrow are proud to support the Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation with the help of our guests and employees. Our funding includes the specific sponsorship of five children, Nhu, Tien, Sang, Hoi, and Ha, so they continue to stay in school, access higher education and hopefully lift themselves and their families out of poverty. The oldest student OneTomorrow currently sponsors, Nhu is just one example of the incredible impact Blue Dragon has for young people. At age 15, she is excelling in Maths and Literature and aspires to become a psychologist and support her Mum and little sister, a stark contrast from what her life would have looked like had she been forced to leave school to work. With OneTomorrow’s continued support, even more children can experience the joy and security of education, with all costs covered.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Donates Over $500,000 in 2022
posts.body:
From little things, big things grow. ATGs charitable fund OneTomorrow has had an incredible year, furthering our mission as a company to have an enduring positive impact on the nature and communities we touch. We achieve our vision by promoting a more sustainable and socially aware way of travelling, by partnering with grassroots and community-led charities in the places we travel to and educating our guests on tour about their vital work.

In 2022 OneTomorrow has donated over $500,000 to our associated charities, part of which was generously donated by our guests through the OneTomorrow guest giving program. Guests can donate to their chosen partner charity and OneTomorrow will double the donation. OneTomorrow is delighted to have supported 18 charities this year, from providing specific grants, to hosting fundraising events.

Here is a snapshot of the impact OneTomorrow has had this year:


Flood Relief – Australia

We are all aware of the devastation caused to communities across Australia by the recent floods. Farmland and crops have been destroyed, and after the extreme bush fires of previous years, farmers are struggling to bounce back yet again.

As an Australian-owned business we see it as our responsibility to support our regional workers and have worked closely with organisations working to help flood-effected areas recover. Through Rural Aid, Mooroopna CFA and The Salvation Army we have donated $30,000 towards flood relief, which has been used to supply emergency accommodation and food, as well as counselling for impacted families.


Free Education – Cambodia

Travellers who have enjoyed an APT tour to Siem Reap in Cambodia will be familiar with ODA (Opportunities for Development thru Art) and the eight free schools they operate. Subsistence farming is still the way of life for many families in Cambodia, and a large number of children from regional communities end up working on farms rather than attending school.

ODA proudly helps create opportunities for children by providing free English language and computer classes in the outlying villages of Siem Reap. Being fluent in English and having computer skills are key to improving employment opportunities in the local tourism and government sector, hence lifting families out of poverty.

This year OneTomorrow donated $50,000 to support ODA’s programs, helping bringing quality education to Cambodia’s most underprivileged.


Life-changing medical treatment – Germany

ATG has been cruising through Germany for over 20 years, and have built a special relationship with Peace Village International. Peace Village International is a remarkable organisation that fly children from war-torn states to Germany to receive vital medical treatment and rehabilitation not available in their home countries. From Uzbekistan to Uganda, Peace Village International’s greatest challenge is finding appropriately equipped transport for severely injured and unwell children, which may include specifically chartered flights.

With our donation,Peace Village International were able to safely transport 123 sick or wounded children to the Peace Village, Dusseldorf where a team of physios, surgeons, doctors, and nurses were on hand to provide specialist treatment. After receiving the care they so desperately needed, all the children are also provided flights home to be reunited with their families, healthier and happier.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Donates $7,500 to Rainforest 4 Foundation
posts.body:
Estimated to be approximately 180 million years old, the Daintree Rainforest is one of the worlds oldest rainforests, and at 1,200 square kilometres (or 296,526 acres), this stunning expanse of forest plays a vital role in the Australian ecosystem. However, like so many natural wonders, the Daintree has suffered significant deforestation over recent decades, and without intervention we risk losing many indigenous Queensland flora, fauna and animals. Fortunately, the Not-for-Profit organisation Rainforest 4 Foundation is committed to conserving the rainforest for future generations and is gradually buying back the rainforests surrounding land to create protected areas with the hope of re-planting native trees and expanding the Daintree.


Last year, OneTomorrow were delighted to help fund the acquisition of additional acres for Rainforest 4, and this month, OneTomorrow made a further donation of $7,500 towards the cost of planting 1,000 trees on the newly acquired land. This particular planting project will focus on restoring the habitat for the native Southern Cassowary, which has been labelled a Threatened species due to past de-forestation. The cost of planting a tree in the Daintree - which includes site preparation, digging holes, securing plants grown from local provenance seeds, and maintaining the planting - is $10 per tree.


OneTomorrow would like to extend a thank you to all who donated so generously to help restore the rainforest ecosystem. We look forward to continuing our partnership with the Rainforest 4 Foundation and protecting the Daintree Rainforest for generations to come.

OneTomorrow Champions Sustainability Onboard Travelmarvels European River Ships, earning Green Award Status.

Travelmarvel’s latest fleet of Contemporary River Ships is leading the way in sustainable tourism practices, earning Green Award status. From ensuring catering staff are trained in food waste reduction, to removing single-use plastic from cruises, OneTomorrow and Travelmarvel are constantly looking for opportunities to reduce the companies carbon footprint and protect our environment for future generations. Read below the initiatives implemented on Travelmarvels European cruises.

Recycling and Reusing Plastic

Rather than opt for single-use products, we have invested in high quality cleaning materials, which can be washed and reused. Even something as simple as substituting single use plastic gloves for rubber cleaning gloves can dramatically reduce the amount of plastic destined landfill. Any plastics which cannot be repurposed onboard Travelmarvel ships are deposited at plastic recycling units rather than placed in general waste.

Removing One-Use Items

A small, but significant change in our fight to reduce waste has been removing all single-use plastic water bottles from tours. Fortunately, Travelmarvel guests have been all too happy to bring their own reusable water bottles, which can be used at the water stations placed throughout our River Ships and available 24/7.

We have also substituted small single-use wash products with refillable receptacles’, meaning product containers can be used for years on our cruises, rather than just one week.


Reducing Waste

An estimated 70% of food thrown away globally is perfectly usable, and at OneTomorrow, we want to ensure this troubling statistic isn’t representative of our food wastage on tour. The catering team onboard our European River Cruises have all participated in a recognised food waste saving program and have implemented best practices on tour to ensure wastage is kept to an absolute minimum. This includes ensuring our kitchens do not over produce and our team keep a diligent record of food usage to identify ways to further reduce waste.

posts.title: How can ice help answer our climate questions?
posts.body:
This Earth Day, OneTomorrow Charitable Fund shines a light on the incredible contribution made by Antarctic Science Foundation in researching our climate.


Later this year, an Antarctic expedition will venture South to drill an ice core dating back more than a million years. This project will require an inland trek of over 1,300 kilometres from the coast to establish a remote drill site and camp to house equipment and researchers over the summer months.


The goal is ambitious in scale but will make a vital contribution to the climate puzzle. Within this rare ice are tiny bubbles that act as pockets containing air and chemicals captured throughout time. Analysis of these gases and chemicals will provide a snapshot of the Earth’s climate and atmospheric composition. Researchers can use this information to make more accurate predictions of climate stability and help us understand the strategies required to mitigate the effects of climate disruption.


Other climate initiatives Antarctic Science Foundation contribute to:

• Climate prediction for all Australians.

• Fire, flood and drought prediction and mitigation.

• Managing economic and sustainable fisheries.

• Carbon capture and abatement via nature’s systems.

• Increasing the health of our oceans.

• Improving global biodiversity.

• Protection of Antarctic wildlife.

posts.title: How football can change a child’s life.
posts.body:
Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation have rescued over 1,000 people from slavery, helped 6,000 kids back to school and assisted more than 600 homeless children reunite with their families. But there is another figure that is equally important for Blue Dragon and that’s having played over 3,000 football games with local children in the streets of Vietnam.


Football has been a large part of the organisation from the beginning.


Nam was one of these kids who came to Blue Dragon in the organisations early days. He didn’t want help going back to school because he needed money to support his mother and younger brothers in the countryside. Blue Dragon learnt of his passion for football and invited him to weekly games.


After a year of participating in football games, Nam trusted the organisation to seek for help. He needed help finding a job as money was a priority to his family, Blue Dragon understood and introduced him to Donald Berger, one of Hanoi’s best restaurateurs. Nam’s life changed forever.


Nam is now an award-winning chef who worked part time at Blue Dragon for many years, but now finds himself as head chef for a company with seven restaurants. It is astonishing how a weekly football game was able to positively impact Nam’s life.


If you’d like to help children like Nam, please donate to Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation today. OneTomorrow is a proud supporter of the organisation and is committee to doubling each donation received. Please click the donation link here.

posts.title: Highlighting Water First on World Water Day
posts.body:
In celebration of World Water Day, OneTomorrow is recognising the important work that our charity partner, Water First, undertakes in Indigenous communities across Canada.

World Water Day has been celebrated on the 22 of March since 1993. It highlights the importance of accessible drinking water and sustainable management of freshwater resources.

In numerous Indigenous communities across Canada, tap water is not safe to drink. The water challenges faced by many Indigenous communities in Canada are complex. Some communities are concerned about infrastructure, whereas some do not have the capacity to train people in operating and maintaining systems to ensure safe, clean water. Safe water needs skilled people.

In January, One Tomorrow donated $5,000 to Water First, which in turn OneTomorrow’s donations provided Indigenous communities with the opportunity to participate in Water First’s Drinking Water Internship Program. The program supports young Indigenous adults to become certified water treatment plant operators in 15 months. With over 50,000 hours of hands-on training in water treatment plants to date, the long term affects within Indigenous communities are changing lives.


We are proud to continue donating to Water First. If you’d like to learn more about the charity and their ongoing work, please visit their website here.

posts.title: OneTomorrow donates $20,000 to Australian flood support

posts.title: OneTomorrow Supports Downtown Eastside Women’s Centre’s events
posts.body:
OneTomorrow are proud to support Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside Women’s Centre (DEWC) who have been providing refuge to women and children since 1978. Aiding local women with shelter, crisis relief, and basic necessities, DEWC offers practical support to impact the lives of over 700 women and children every day.

Recently OneTomorrow contributed $6,000 to DEWC’s annual Christmas event, which provided 450 meals and Christmas gift bags to attendees.

The event was held on Columbia Street in front of the Drop-In Centre which was closed specifically for the event. With a large tent set up complete with fairy lights and rows of dinner tables, women were able to come by and enjoy a warm holiday meal, courtesy of APT Travel Group and OneTomorrow. Volunteer musicians contributed with festive songs while all staff got into the spirit be wearing their favourite Christmas attire.

OneTomorrow will continue to support DEWC’s efforts to expand their Meals Program. These meals are an essential part of the basic needs provided at DEWC’s Drop-In Centre and emergency shelters. Since July 1, 2021, they have seen a 50% increase in the number of women accessing their services; and for many of these women, a meal at DEWC is their only nutrition for the day. They currently serve 750 meals per day and an expansion of our Meals Program will allow them to continue serving the increasing needs of the women in the community.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Sponsors Leopard Sharks
posts.body:
In support of Conservation International’s Leopard Shark Population Recovery Program, OneTomorrow has sponsored 2 sharks and donated $2,000 to the project.

As part of the sponsorship, OneTomorrow held an internal competition to name the Shark duo, asking APT Travel Group staff to submit their suggestions.” The always funny “SharkyMcSharkFace” was floated around, though sense prevailed and the group decided on “Leonie” and “Leonard.”

These sharks were recently tagged off the coast of Stradbroke Island in Queensland, where a team of 6 researchers caught and released these sharks from the shallow waters. The research team included Christine Dudgeon from University of Queensland who is a world-renowned expert in leopard sharks and has been studying this population for 18 years.

The tagging will allow researchers to gather data from the sharks for up to 10 years. The knowledge gained will help improve Conservation Internationals shark repopulation program, resulting in successfully hatching and raising more aquaria-sources pups into Raja Ampat. This is a world first attempt to boost a wild population in such a way.

Learn more about Conservation International’s Leopard Shark Population Recovery Program

posts.title: Peace Village International: Providing medical attention to children living in war zones
posts.body:
Since 1967, Peace Village have been working to provide medical attention to children living in war zones. 

The Germany based initiative, ensures children have access to treatment and physiotherapy in European hospitals and rehabilitate approximately 1,000 children each year through the program. They are then returned to their families and homes after healing. 

Peace Village International provide: 

  • Individual medical aid for sick and injured children impacted by war who cannot receive adequate treatment in their home countries.
  • Aid projects in regions of war and conflict to improve local medical services.
  • Peace education to promote humanitarian awareness and social engagement.


OneTomorrow is a long-time supporter of Peace Village International and have donated $7,000 to their important work. This is inclusive of a recent $2,000 one off grant which OneTomorrow provided to Peace Village as part of the annual 2021 grant program.

On top of these grants, APT Travel Group staff will also be participating in a “Race through Europe” challenge this month, which aims to raise more donations for Peace Village. posts.title: Rainforest 4 Purchase Portion of Daintree Rainforest with the help of OneTomorrow
posts.body:
Thanks to generous donations from several organisations, including OneTomorrow, Rainforest 4 Foundation have recently purchased 9 hectares of the Daintree Rainforest, preserving a small portion of this invaluable eco-system for another generation.

The Daintree Lowland Rainforest is one of the oldest rainforests on Earth having survived undisturbed for over 120 million years. It holds exceptionally high biodiversity and conservation value and is the largest continuous area of tropical rainforest remaining in Australia. Due to extensive deforestation, the forest and the rare and endangered species living there are under threat.

The recent lot purchases total 11 properties secured by Rainforest 4 Foundation, who work collaboratively with Jabalbina Yalanji Aboriginal Corporation and non-profit partner HalfCut. Securing these lots means that these areas will not be impacted by development and will aid the protection of threatened species including Southern Cassowary, Bennett’s Tree-Kangaroo, and seven species of plants.

You can help support Rainforest 4 Foundation and help return the Daintree Rainforest to its former glory. A $50 donation will buy back 20 square metres of the Daintree Rainforest. More information can be found through our Rainforest 4 Foundation page.

posts.title: OneTomorrow donates $12,000 to Royal Flying Doctor Service
posts.body:
OneTomorrow recently made a $12,000 donation to the Royal Flying Doctor Service to aid mental health services. The donation was presented by two groups of Captain's Choice guests as they visited the Broken Hill Royal Flying Doctor Service on an outback private plane tour.

Access to mental health services is not equal for families in remote, rural, and regional Australia and the Flying Doctor bridges the gap by delivering services to communities that would otherwise go without.

posts.title: Royal Flying Doctor Service: Guardians of the Sky
posts.body:
Of all the iconic outback institutions Australia is blessed with, the Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) is surely one of the first that comes to mind. Connecting our rural residents to vital healthcare services, the RFDS has been saving lives for more than 90 years. Utilising its own fleet of aircraft, the RFDS ensures distance need not be a reason for people missing out on the benefits of the latest medical technology.

Operating in some of Australia’s most remote areas, APT’s Kimberley & Outback Wilderness Adventures (KOWA) has a close working relationship with the RFDS. On occasion, KOWA has been the beneficiary of their essential services, such as when needing to address the health concerns of its guests. It’s comforting to know they can quickly respond if needed and that the impressive scope of their operations takes in even the most far-off regions of our country.

All of KOWA’s Driver Guides engage in fundraising for the RFDS while on tour. A stand-out in that area has been Gary Annett, who has managed to raise an incredible $66,000 for the RFDS since 2016 through photographic calendar sales alone.

With a third of its operating budget being dependent on fundraising, philanthropy and corporate partnerships, the RFDS relies largely on the generosity of the community to continue delivering its high quality of service, which sees it continue to help 1,000 people each day.

While it is largely known for its fleet of aircraft, the RFDS also utilises 140 healthcare road vehicles and delivers a wide range of services including GP and nurse clinics, dental, Telehealth, and mental health and wellbeing services.

One of the little known, yet critical aspects of its work involves the stocking of 3,500 medical chests, strategically distributed among tourist venues, general stores, post offices, and other venues throughout Australia. These mini-pharmacies contain such life-preserving items as snakebite kits, antibiotics, painkillers, and defibrillators.

OneTomorrow is proud of its association with the Royal Flying Doctor Service, recognising the great value it brings to the wider community, as well as the importance of supporting its crucial work.

posts.title: Wunan Foundation: Breaking the Cycle
posts.body:
The Wunan Foundation works to give the Aboriginal people of the East Kimberley access to the opportunities they need to live independent and fulfilling lives. Wunan uses the metaphor of swimming the river to illustrate the challenges faced by Aboriginal people as they navigate their way to employment and housing via the education system.

Historically, one of the biggest obstacles to accessing these opportunities has been a general lack of expectation from successive governments, as well as the wider community. This has led to Aboriginal people becoming stuck in the welfare trap, with many also developing a dependence on alcohol and drugs. Domestic violence, mental illness and suicide have also proven depressing outcomes, arising all too often from this cycle of disadvantage.

It’s estimated that around 60 per cent of children in the region miss the necessary parental support to obtain the opportunities that would break this cycle. It’s these children who now benefit from Wunan’s specialised programs.

Through their Pathway to Home Ownership program, Wunan assists those looking to buy or build a home, while also providing skills in financial literacy. Support is also given to people wishing to access Kununurra’s public housing via the Move to Town initiative, while the Financial Capability Hub helps Aboriginal people to develop their overall money management skills.

The Parent & Community Engagement program encourages parents to engage with their child’s school and support their learning at home. Driver Training Programs in Kununurra and Halls Creek provide the skills needed to assist Aboriginal people to obtain employment. Wunan also operates a medical practice, a business support service and even a wholly Aboriginal-owned and operated Bed and Breakfast.

The challenges the Wunan Foundation is helping Aboriginal people to overcome are summarised in the short video ‘Swimming the River’, narrated by Wunan’s Chairman, Ian Trust. You can watch the video here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0P9FRacTji0

OneTomorrow was grateful for the time Wunan’s Eddy Gaskill, Amanda Fernando and Dr Stephanie Trust recently gave. Their online visit offered OneTomorrow and the wider ATG family further insight into the nature of the problems, solutions and opportunities being worked through on a daily basis in the East Kimberley.

posts.title: In Support of Longer, Healthier Lives For Australia’s Men
posts.body:
The clock is ticking. Every hour in Australia, at least four men die from preventable diseases, leaving a devasting impact on the lives of their families and the wider community.

At every stage of life, the rates of mortality for cancer, diabetes and diseases of the circulatory system are higher for men than for women. We see their effects compounded with 74 per cent of alcohol-related deaths also occurring in men, while more than two-thirds of Australian men are overweight or obese. A large number also experience depression at some point in their life. As with all health-related issues, awareness and early diagnosis are key.

The importance of addressing these issues resonated with the committee, and OneTomorrow recently had the pleasure of hearing from Professor Gary Richardson, who sits on the board of Foundation 49: Men’s Health. Created in honour of the late journalist Tony Hitchin, the foundation’s vision is to enable men to live longer and healthier lives. A respected oncologist, Professor Richardson spoke about how modern scientific and medical research is making it easier than ever before for men to become informed about their specific health concerns.

By focusing on conditions that may occur during each stage of life, Foundation 49 educates men on the causes, as well as respective prevention and treatment options. Key risk factors for men can include drinking too much alcohol, falling prey to depression and self-harm while in their twenties, and becoming too sedentary in their later years.

A major component of the foundation’s work also involves helping men to take an active interest in their reproductive and sexual health. It achieves this through providing evidence-based information that is inclusive of everyone, regardless of education, religion or ethnicity.

As part of his presentation, Professor Richardson explained how everyone has a stake in the improvement of men’s health. Partners, families, employers and the wider community benefit from an overall increase in men’s health status.

Recognising the importance of supporting a cause that represents 49 per cent of the community, OneTomorrow reached out to Professor Richardson and Foundation 49 to contribute a $2,000 donation. These funds will further enable the valuable not-for-profit to continue its work promoting health and wellbeing to men of all ages.

posts.title: $20,000 Donation to Rural Aid to Support Aussie Farmers
posts.body:
In the early hours of the morning on 30th December 2019, an uncontrollable blaze swept through a family farm near Cudgewa in northeast Victoria, leaving a path of devastation in its wake.

Lynne, a staff member of the APT Travel Group (ATG), grew up on a farm near the Snowy Mountains, a farm which has been owned by her family for four generations. Stretching across over 400 hectares of both hill and flat country, the farm was home to woolly sheep grazing on the hills, while bellowing cattle took up residence along the flats.

2019 marked the beginning of Australia’s worst bushfire season to date. More than 7.3 million hectares of land was destroyed, including Lynne’s family’s farm. Already on high alert after the fire warnings, Lynne, who was staying at the farm at the time, was able to transport her family to safety before the fires hit. Meanwhile, her brother and father stayed behind to courageously defend their home.

Their tenacity and strength saved the family home, the shearing shed and the machinery shed. However, the rest of the farm was completely obliterated. 95% of the land was burnt and blackened, almost all fences were destroyed, the old dairy gone, the original farm homestead was ruined along with irreplaceable photos, furniture and mementos, and a third of their beautiful animals had lost their lives.

Lynne’s father and brother were lucky to escape with their lives. It was a miracle both came out of the fight with no more than singed eyelids and superficial burns. However, leaving a scar are the memories of the moment when the fire hit.

The aftermath has proved even more of a hardship. The rest of the community were tending to their own destroyed properties, so Lynne and her family were on their own. Water supplies were polluted by the smoke, surviving livestock were severely traumatised, and all pasture grass had been burnt, so there was no food for the animals.

Lynne recalls the first moment she was able to drive into the farm once the smoke had cleared. “It felt like someone was squeezing my heart. The destruction the fire caused is not something I can describe except to say, everything was so very black.”

Fast forwarding five months on, the farm is starting to come back to life. After some decent rainfall, green has begun to sprout. Some pasture grasses have recovered, and after receiving a hay donation from Rural Aid, the livestock have food to eat.

In May 2020, OneTomorrow made a $20,000 donation to Rural Aid, who will be using a portion of this donation to support Lynne and her family through this difficult time.

“The amount of work that we have done so far is enormous. The amount of work still to do is unbelievable,” says Lynne. Weeks upon weeks have been spent repairing the fences, with no end in sight. Lynne’s father, at 79 years of age, has shown a tremendous effort to return his farm to its former glory. In the months since the fires hit, he has had only two days of rest. He, like many other farmers in a similar situation, will receive much-needed support from Rural Aid, which will play a part in the immense task of getting the farm back on track.

The kindness shown by complete strangers helps spur Lynne and her family on. “I would like to take this opportunity to thank OneTomorrow and all the ATG staff who support OneTomorrow, who have shown such generosity to my family,” says Lynne.

posts.title: Empowering Local Communities Through Education
posts.body:
Creating opportunities for young people to grow and prosper is a key component of the change OneTomorrow is striving to bring about in the world.

With the APT Travel Group (ATG) having a long history in Western Australia’s Kimberley region, we are mindful of many of the issues faced by Aboriginal people there. The Kimberley is known to have one of the highest rates of suicide in the world, with the region’s young people being particularly vulnerable.

Education is the most important means by which to empower and create resilient children. The OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is making a noticeable difference in the Kimberley, having recently contributed $14,000 to the Kandiwal Community. This donation has made the possibility of hiring a part-time teacher a reality. While the School of the Air remains the main source of education for the children, being equipped to offer students face-to-face learning is an important step in providing a more positive future.

As OneTomorrow’s Madeleine Curtain says: ‘Equitable and quality education is an important sustainability goal of the United Nations and is a key focus of OneTomorrow’s community work around the world’. Increasing the access to education, while ensuring that learning keeps pace with technology, is fundamental to improving the wellbeing of individuals and communities.

Located in a highly remote part of the Kimberley, the Kandiwal community are members of the Wunambal people, who welcome visitors to Ngauwudu (Mitchell Plateau). It is here that APT’s Mitchell Falls Wilderness Lodge provides a touch of luxury in the wilderness for its guests.

Building upon the relationships APT has developed with local Indigenous communities, through its Kimberley Wilderness Adventures, OneTomorrow will continue to roll out a range of initiatives in support of the Kimberley and its people.
