posts.title: A Lifeline For a Vital Community Service
posts.body:
Recall the difficulties and inconveniences you’ve had to work through during the recent lockdown. Now imagine having to negotiate those challenges while living in one of the most remote parts of the Kimberley, where keeping a business running smoothly proves a challenge in the best of times.

The Imintji Community Store provides basic amenities, grocery items and fuel, among other necessary goods and services. Located on the legendary Gibb River Road, it is a key resource for travellers to the area, while being an essential part of the community; offering a source of employment, an outlet for local arts and crafts, and supplying necessities for locals. 

Having an intimate knowledge of the region, APT staff soon became aware that the store was in danger of closing. Reaching out to OneTomorrow, a much-needed contribution of $10,000 was subsequently made in support of this essential community hub.

‘The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 10 encourages us to support the marginalised and the disadvantaged’, OneTomorrow Charitable Fund Manager Madeleine Curtain explained, ‘and so when we were told about the Imintji Community Store, we could not allow such a valuable community asset to perish.’

The Imintji (Ngarinyin) people invite guests to experience the spectacular King Leopold Ranges. Here, APT’s Bell Gorge Wilderness Lodge offers easy access to Bell, Windjana, Galvans and Barnett River Gorges, as well as Tunnel Creek. In fact, its location presents as the ideal base for exploring most of the key highlights of the western portion of the Kimberley.

APT has enjoyed an evolving  relationship with the Imintji community over the last 16 years, as a result of the brand’s Kimberley Wilderness Adventures, which operates in the area. Where possible, APT seeks to employ local staff, and also provides space at Bell Gorge Wilderness Lodge for local Imintji artists to display and sell their work.

OneTomorrow looks to ensure the survival and ongoing viability of the Imintji Community Store, as it continues to serve the local community and provide a welcome rest stop for visitors to the Kimberley.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Donates to an OzChild Carer In Need
posts.body:
We are brought together through generosity and community.

The APT Travel Group (ATG) raised money for OzChild last Christmas, a donation which was matched by the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund. Rallied by APT Travel Group staff member Patrice, a fantastic toy drive for Christmas was held in support of OzChild, the leading child welfare organisation, who are dedicated to improving the lives of at-risk children, young people and families in the community.

On receiving the donation, OzChild decided that the best way to use it was to support a kinship carer. In Pakenham, a carer looking after nine children was facing challenges every day. One of those challenges affected the day-to-day running of the home. The carer’s small, unreliable washing machine meant that in a household of 10, the carer’s small, unreliable washing machine simply couldn’t keep up with the ever-growing pile of laundry. The carer was struggling to get through a minimum of 20 loads every week.

Alison, the case worker supporting the carer, suggested the best way to spend this donation was by replacing this insufficient washing machine with a bigger and better model. The new 14.5kg washing machine was found at Harvey Norman Springvale in Victoria. Harvey Norman and the supplier kindly agreed to offer the appliance at below cost and the donation from OneTomorrow was used to purchase the washing machine.

“The carer was so excited about the washing machine!” says Alison. “She choked back tears as she told me how much easier it was going to be for her now.”

Alison shares that during her visit to the carer’s home, the carer’s excitement had spread to the children. They made sure to show Alison the new washing machine as soon as she stepped foot through the door.
 
“The carer said doing the washing for 10 people was taking her hours and hours every week, and she never felt like she was on top of it,” says Alison. “She asked to have her thanks passed onto everyone for this amazingly generous gift.”

Patrice was unable to operate the Easter raffle this year due to Covid-19 social distancing restrictions, so OneTomorrow made a further donation of $2,000 to OzChild in May 2020.

posts.title: Long-Standing Partners of APT Travel Group (ATG) Support Bushfire Relief
posts.body:
In the wake of disaster, hope can spring from the most unexpected of places.

2019 saw the beginnings of Australia’s worst bushfire season to date with fires burning well into the new year. The devastation rallied Australians to raise money to support those affected by the natural disaster, as well as emergency services and volunteer organisations.

This compassion extended beyond our borders, to our friends over in Vietnam and Cambodia. Those who, while not directly affected by the fires, felt the nation’s pain as though it was their own.

Donations were raised by the staff at Focus Travel Vietnam and Focus Travel Cambodia, long-standing travel partners of APT Travel Group (ATG). In addition, current and former Tour Directors and local guides also donated what they could. Together, the Vietnam and Cambodia team raised an incredible $3,500 AUD.

Special mentions must be made of Focus Travel Cambodia, who responded instantly to the cause. Also, to Focus Travel Vietnam’s director Minh and employee Nhan, who were the driving forces behind the wonderful effort made by the Vietnam office.

When asked, staff of Focus Travel Vietnam were emphatic that this was all Nhan’s initiative. From a young age, Nhan has lived by the popular Vietnamese proverb, “When you eat the fruit, be grateful to the planter.” It’s all about a mindful way of living with gratitude. Now, as a mother of two, Nhan’s philanthropic ethos is mirrored by her two children. Often, Nhan and her sons visit children’s centres to show their support for kids in need.

Described as having a heart “as big as a whale”, upon seeing much of Australia in a state of emergency, and holding a deep appreciation for APT Travel Group (ATG) as her employer, Nhan felt she had to help. So, after mobilising her colleagues and inspiring Minh, Nhan was able to pull together an impressive portion of the overall donation.

Minh made the largest contribution on behalf of Focus Travel Vietnam, by pledging to triple all donations raised by the Vietnam office. Minh will be in the Melbourne APT Travel Group (ATG) office on 17th February to personally hand in the money raised by the Cambodia and Vietnam offices.

Our gratitude towards Nhan and our friends over in Vietnam and Cambodia cannot be expressed enough. Generosity shown by those who, despite low wages and the oceans of distance between them and the bushfires, still rallied together for a country in crisis and opened their hearts.


Minh personally made the journey to Jingellic, one of the most fire-ravaged parts of NSW. Here, he witnessed a Rural Aid hay drop, and distributed the money raised by Focus Travel Vietnam and Focus Travel Cambodia. By doing this, he was able to see the positive impact the donations had to support this town who were desperately in need of hay to feed their livestock.

posts.title: Bushfire Relief Fundraising at APT Travel Group (ATG)
posts.body:
2019 marked the beginnings of the worst bushfire season Australia has seen in decades. Entire towns have been destroyed, half a billion animals affected and more than 7.3 million hectares of land burned.

In support of bushfire relief, a number of staff fundraising events were held at APT Travel Group (ATG) on 15th January 2020. These included a second-hand clothing recycle boutique, a sausage sizzle lunch, raffle prizes and gold coin donations.

Contributions through these events were matched by OneTomorrow, garnering some fantastic end results.

$10,100 was raised in just a single day, thanks to the generosity of staff donations and the matched OneTomorrow funding.

In addition to the $132,000 which had previously been donated by the APT Travel Group (ATG) and OneTomorrow, this brings us to an outstanding contribution of $143,100 towards bushfire relief.

The generosity and dedication shown by APT Travel Group's (ATG) staff towards this cause has been uplifting, and OneTomorrow would like to recognise everyone who was involved in the effort.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Scores at 2019 Workplace Giving Awards
posts.body:
It’s with great pride that we announce the successful recognition of the One Tomorrow Charitable Fund at the 2019 Workplace Giving Excellence Awards.

OneTomorrow has been recognised with a bronze medal for its innovation and commitment to the global community through its staff Workplace Giving program.

The fourth annual awards took place in 2019, recognising the most outstanding workplace giving programs across Australia. In attendance were the Hon Gary Johns Commissioner, the ACNC, and CEOs from the country’s leading business and Not-For-Profit organisations.

Workplace Giving is known to engage employees, improve business performance and have an enormous impact on the community. It’s our chance to make a meaningful contribution to support the OneTomorrow vision.

OneTomorrow’s encouragement of Workplace Giving was demonstrated by offering to triple staff donations for those who signed up in August for the first three months, and matching staff donations thereafter.

All funds raised through the program, which continues to grow in its success, go towards local charity partners selected by our body of staff.

posts.title: OneTomorrow Donates $10,000 to Blue Dragon
posts.body:
$10,000 has been donated to Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation, as one of OneTomorrow’s chosen grassroots causes. Blue Dragon offers children and families in northern Vietnam who are in crisis the chance to turn their lives around, providing care, shelter, legal advocacy and long-term support.

This donation will ensure Blue Dragon can continue providing children with immediate care and rescue, while long-term change is carried out on a systematic level, affecting law reform, policy developments and training programs.

Blue Dragon has become a powerful force for change on the streets of Vietnam, both in the bustling cities and in rural areas where poverty is widespread. Thanks to their ongoing work, children suffering from rural poverty, disabilities, homelessness, HIV/AIDs and human trafficking are given hope for a better future.

Here at OneTomorrow, we are proud of our relationship with Blue Dragon, whose mission is to give exceptional care to the children who need it most.

About Us

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is an initiative of the APT Travel Group (ATG), a not-for-profit program with a vision to strive for a positive, enduring impact on the nature and communities we touch. This is achieved through immediate and long-term influence in various environmental and humanitarian causes.

Over the years APT Travel Group (ATG) has contributed to and partnered with several worthy charities, both locally and abroad. The OneTomorrow Charitable Fund was created to establish a more formalised approach to these activities.

Making a Difference

Make Travel Mean More

Travel changes us. Whether it’s those small moments that move you, or the lifelong memories you create, journeys can transform how we see the world. At OneTomorrow, we recognise the power that travel has. We want to take it one step further. Working with you and the great causes we support around the world, together we are creating a future where travel means more.

Guest Giving

Our world is a beautiful one, filled with diverse cultures and unique environments. As a guest of the APT Travel Group (ATG), you can now further immerse yourself in the places you visit. OneTomorrow’s Guest Giving program allows you to support worthy projects in different regions around the world, with our matched funding doubling your impact. Our partner organisations are carefully selected to better local communities and the environment.

Grants and Donations

As a family business, the APT Travel Group (ATG) has been driven by its community conscience and strong family values for over 96 years. These values led to the formation of OneTomorrow and are paramount in everything we do. From donating to our charity partners, matching our guests’ donations, supporting regions impacted by disaster and pouring what we can back into the global community, we ensure we live up to our vision as a responsible business.

Workplace Giving

Making a difference starts from the ground up, and our Workplace Giving program encourages charitable giving within the APT Travel Group (ATG). Regular tax-deductible donations from our staff go towards local charities, with funds matched by OneTomorrow. For our efforts, we were awarded the bronze medal at the Australian Workplace Giving Awards, showing the impact we can make on a personal level.

Our Workplace Giving charities, chosen by our staff, include Cancer Council, The Smith Family, Backpack4Kids, Blue Dragon, Royal Flying Doctor Service, Rural Aid, The Salvation Army, STREAT, Australian Animal Protection Society, Beyond Blue, Médecins San Frontiers (Doctors without Borders) and The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne.

Our People

OneTomorrow and the APT Travel Group (ATG) are made up of a team of incredible staff whose personal values shine through in what they do. Volunteer days and staff fundraising initiatives, ranging from office bake sales to raffles, allows us to express our support for causes we feel passionate about. Instigated and run by staff voluntarily, these activities are supported by APT Travel Group and furthered by OneTomorrow’s matched funding.

Background

OneTomorrow's Origin

OneTomorrow has been 21 years in the making, since the APT Travel Group (ATG) first established a philanthropic fund with the Australian Communities Foundation (ACF). Owned and operated by the McGeary family for over 97 years, the APT Travel Group (ATG) has always stood by its social integrity and strong family values. Today, this means delivering guests exceptional journeys globally, while providing meaningful connections and strategic philanthropic investment within the communities they visit. Launched in 2019, OneTomorrow is the resulting philanthropic initiative of the APT Travel Group (ATG).

Our Mission

OneTomorrow strives to have a positive, enduring impact on the nature and communities we touch. Our mission is conscientious travel, and we hope to achieve this by creating an immediate and long-term positive influence on the environmental and humanitarian causes we support. This is achieved through:

  • Connecting the world with sustainable movements.

  • Enhancing and empowering the livelihood of communities.

  • Being leaders in change, and educating through our global business and social reach.

  • Forging meaningful connections between OneTomorrow and our guests that are preserved long after their return home.

Accountability and Governance

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is a not-for-profit sub-fund of the Australian Communities Foundation (ACF: ABN 57967620066) and a partner of Australian NGO, Global Development Group (GDG: ABN 57 102 400 993). Together these provide a formalised, legally compliant framework to ensure donated funds benefit the designated projects.

The Australian Communities Foundation, as a registered Deductible Gift Recipient for tax purposes, manages the money invested by APT Travel Group.

Global Development Group is an Item 1 Deductible Gift Recipient and ACNC-registered charity, a member of the Australian Council for International Development (ACFID) and an approved organisation under DFAT’s Overseas Aid Gift Deduction Scheme, carrying out approved projects overseas with smaller, grassroots in-country project partners around the world.

APT Travel Group (ATG) Brands

Through a comprehensive suite of travel brands, the APT Travel Group (ATG) has pioneered global and domestic travel experiences that cater to everyone. The APT Travel Group (ATG) is comprised of the brands APT, Travelmarvel, Captain’s Choice, Botanica World Discoveries, Antarctica Flights and TravelGlo.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why should I support OneTomorrow?

When you give to OneTomorrow, you make twice as much difference in the world. Donations from you are matched by us, dollar for dollar. This means that, together, we can double our impact across the globe.

What is the relationship between OneTomorrow and the APT Travel Group (ATG)?

OneTomorrow is the charitable fund of the APT Travel Group (ATG). Proudly owned by the McGeary family, the group is comprised of the brands APT, Travelmarvel, TravelGlo, Captain’s Choice, Antarctica Flights and Botanica World Discoveries. Born in 2019, the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund now formalises the history of charitable activities carried out by APT Travel Group (ATG).

How does OneTomorrow select the projects they support?

OneTomorrow seeks out projects in the areas to which we travel to which, through their generosity and selflessness, create an appreciable difference to our environment and the people living within it. Our partner causes must also align with the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.

What are Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and how do they involve OneTomorrow?

The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a global plan of action put forward by the United Nations (UN) to drive peace and prosperity for people and planet. They form the UN’s 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and highlight 17 key areas of focus. We’ve chosen three specific SDGs to address through OneTomorrow: Good Health and Wellbeing; Quality Education; and Life on Land.

Where does the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund get their money from?

The APT Travel Group (ATG) established a philanthropic fund with the Australian Communities Foundation (ACF) in 2005. Since then the company has placed a percentage of its profits each year in the fund. As the fund has grown, so too has the amount of interest earnt. Today, the fund has grown to such a degree that the company uses the interest earnt each year for philanthropic endeavours, now under the header of OneTomorrow.

How do I know my money makes a difference?

The OneTomorrow Charitable Fund is a sub-fund of the Australian Communities Foundation (ACF: ABN 57967620066) and a partner of Global Development Group (GDG: ABN 57 102 400 993); both are registered Deductible Gift Recipient for tax purposes and comply with all Australian legal obligations and are responsible for ensuring the money donated supports the correct ACF or GDG project. The ACF manages the money invested by APT Travel Group.

On OneTomorrow’s end, our passionate and dedicated personnel maintain regular, direct contact with our charitable partners. The most rewarding aspect of our work is witnessing the results of our efforts and their measurable impacts upon those most in need. By selecting the News tab on our website, you can also keep up to date on all of the latest developments resulting from OneTomorrow’s work.

Is my donation tax-deductible?

All donations to OneTomorrow (as a sub-fund of ACF and thanks to our project partnership with GDG) are eligible as tax-deductible gifts for Australian and United States ($2 and over), and New Zealand citizens ($5 and over) donating in their local currency. As required by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) we advise that if any causes are over-supported that funds may support other approved causes. For European and United Kingdom citizens, we can provide you with an acknowledgement of the donation.

Are there any fees on my donation?

Staff costs for OneTomorrow are covered by APT Touring Group. OneTomorrow does not deduct any costs from your donation.


You may tick the optional amount box when you donate to cover the fundraising costs associated with the Raisely website platform. This is optional and does not impact the amount a cause receives.

Can I donate if I live overseas?

Absolutely! As part of a global travel company, OneTomorrow encourages donations from all over the world.

How can I update my details?

To update your details please contact info@aptouring.com.au

I’ve signed up online for an ongoing monthly donation. What date will my donations come out of my account?

Your recurring donation will come out of your account on the same day of the month that you set up your initial donation (give or take a few business days).

How do I change or cancel my ongoing monthly donations?

On the email receipt you receive each month, simply click on the ‘manage my donation’ button. This will give you the option to change or cancel your recurring donation.

Does OneTomorrow have a refund policy?

OneTomorrow does not have a refund policy. All donations are made in good faith and as such are non-refundable. If your donation has been processed in error, please contact us as soon as possible so that we can work with you to address the issue. info@onetomorrow.com.au

Can I leave a bequest for the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund?

Yes, you can. Bequests make a great difference to the projects we support. As a first step, it is recommended you seek qualified legal advice when creating or updating a Will. If you do want to make a bequest to us, you may wish to use the below wording as a guide.

I give [type of gift] to Australian Communities Foundation Limited, as Trustee of Australian Communities Foundation Fund (ABN 57 967 620 066) to be held on trust in the Australian Communities Foundation Fund and request, without obligation, the Trustee of the Fund hold the bequest in the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund and to apply the funds as the Trustee decides/in favour of [name of one of OneTomorrow Charitable Fund’s select causes] purposes and to acknowledge grants from the OneTomorrow Charitable Fund, wherever practical in the Trustee’s discretion. The executor may accept a receipt from the secretary of the Trustee of the Fund as sufficient discharge for this gift.

Examples of types of gift:
A bequest is the gift of an asset or other right provided as part of a Will, intestacy or settlement. Bequests may be for a particular asset, amount or percentage of an estate.

There are several different types of bequests:

  • Pecuniary bequest: a fixed amount specified in a Will.

  • Residuary bequest: the remaining value of an estate when all other bequests to family and friends have been made and liabilities have been paid.

  • Reversionary bequest: allows a surviving partner to benefit from your estate during their lifetime and then for the balance of the estate to be paid to Australian Communities Foundation upon their death.


For further advice, please consult a qualified legal practitioner.

Responsible Travel

What is Responsible Travel?

The world is waking up to the need for more sustainable ways of travelling, and here at OneTomorrow we understand we have a responsibility to our planet. Responsible travel is all about being socially and culturally aware, minimising our environmental footprint and travelling in a way that takes into consideration the locals, environment and individual cultures. We encourage this sustainable way of travel through journeys with the APT Travel Group (ATG).

The UN defines the responsible traveller as one who keeps an open mind towards new cultures and traditions. They respect human rights. They participate in activities which safeguard natural environments. And responsible travellers will buy local goods to contribute to social and economic development.

Our Guiding Principles

Our vision of conscientious travel involves protecting the environment, respecting local communities and ensuring the wellbeing of the individuals within those communities.

As part of our commitment to achieving this, we have embraced the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The SDGs address the global challenges we face, and present a set plan to achieve a fair and sustainable future for everyone. In order to make a more powerful impact, we will begin by focussing on the three SDGs listed below. Our ultimate vision is to incorporate more goals with time in order to attain our shared aspiration for a better future.

Good Health and Wellbeing

Improving access to essential health services; addressing the burden of non-communicable diseases, including mental health; and stepping up the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

Quality Education

Increasing proficiency in reading and mathematics; ensuring quality of education keeps pace with technological advancement; and improving learning outcomes, particularly for women, girls and marginalised individuals.

Life on the Land

Halt and reverse land degradation; preserve and restore biodiversity; and protect endangered species from the threat of extinction.

Our Responsible Travel Commitments

The APT Travel Group (ATG) cares about giving its guests unforgettable journeys – ones that benefit everyone involved. Here at OneTomorrow, we endorse various initiatives across the company, working together so you can travel with the assurance that the places you visit are impacted positively. Below is a snapshot of the various initiatives we are running.

Supporting Indigenous Communities in the Kimberley

An Advanced Ecotourism certificate in the Kimberley speaks volumes about the commitment APT Travel Group (ATG) and OneTomorrow have to maintain our long-standing Indigenous partnerships in Australia. Some of our areas of work include creating sustainable employment opportunities and making donations to the local communities.

Reducing Plastic Waste on Tour

For each minute of every single day, the equivalent of a truckload of plastic enters our world’s waterways. The APT Travel Group (ATG) is committed to changing this. From July 2019, all single-use plastic bottles have been removed on APT and Travelmarvel Mekong and Irrawaddy river cruises. Brand-new Travelmarvel ships on Europe’s waterways are now fitted with environmental water stations. And on our APT Small Ships, refillable water bottles are provided to all guests. Each day, we continue to work with our suppliers in the effort to eliminate single-use plastic bottles in other areas on tour.

Respecting Local Cultures

Throughout journeys with APT Travel Group (ATG), we place a heavy importance on respecting the rights, history, culture and dignity of local and Indigenous people, wherever we go. Encountering local cultures is often the highlight of travelling the world, and it’s important as visitors that we honour them.

Plant-a-Tree Scheme

We’ve reduced the amount of paper used company-wide, choosing to go digital wherever possible. We envision a future where guests on tour with APT Travel Group (ATG) will be able to opt to receive their travel documents electronically. When you choose to go paper-free, OneTomorrow will plant a tree in bushfire-stricken communities. This way, we can help support a more sustainable future.

OneTomorrow Charitable Fund

By forming OneTomorrow, APT Travel Group (ATG) are taking the necessary steps towards responsible travel, continually finding ways to move closer to the ultimate goal of sustainability. Through guest and workplace giving programs, and a range of fundraising efforts, we are collectively working to help people and places around the world.

Antarctic Science Foundation

Antarctica

The Antarctic Science Foundation’s ultimate mission is to protect our planet. This Australian-based charity funds critical research to understand and protect Antarctica in order to help the world prepare and adapt to climate change, now and for generations to come.

The Problem

Antarctica is experiencing major warming due to climate change. This wild continent feels the effects of climate change faster than the rest of the planet, and Antarctica’s wildlife – including penguins, whales and seals – are particularly vulnerable to this. Climate science undertaken in Antarctica is the key to understanding our global climate future.

The Solution

Regular donations ensure funding of critical research into climate change and Antarctica’s wildlife and oceans. With the development of innovative technology and working with some of the world’s top Antarctic scientists, Antarctic Science Foundation can continue their work protecting wildlife and making accurate predictions of global climate.

What difference will your money make?

$50 provides DNA diet analysis to study penguin’s foraging habits.

$200 can analyse seawater to assess the effects of climate change on plankton.

$1,000 purchases one probe to collect data about the changing Antarctic environment from the deep ocean.

$6,000 builds one new wildlife monitoring camera.

Donation Policy

All donations are received subject to our site privacy policy below. All donations over $2 to approved aid and development projects are tax deductible in Australia (and in the USA and (over $5) New Zealand).

The Australian Tax Office (ATO) requires: 1. If funds raised exceed the requirement for any project, the funds may be directed to another project, 2. Tax deductible donations are required to be unconditional gifts and accordingly OneTomorrow Charitable Fund, Global Development Group or Australian Communities Foundation cannot always guarantee that a donor’s preference will be granted.

Please note that no non-development activities (evangelism, welfare or political activities) are funded by, or are a part of OneTomorrow aid and development projects. If, in their own time, OneTomorrow staff, committee, volunteers and contractors of partner organisations undertake or participate in evangelism, proselytism and missionary work, partisan political activities or welfare, they must ensure that their activities are not perceived or viewed as being on behalf of or representative of OneTomorrow Charitable Fund.

You may view the ACF Privacy Policy here. https://www.communityfoundation.org.au/policies/privacy

You may view the GDG Privacy Policy here: https://globaldevelopmentgroup.org/au/help/site-user-policy/

MANAGEMENT OF PERSONAL INFORMATION

At APT, we recognise the importance of your privacy and understand your concerns about the security of the personal information you provide to us. This privacy policy explains how we use any personal information we collect about you, and your rights to access and correct the personal information we hold about you.


In this policy, APT means the entities within the APT Travel Group, including Australian Pacific Touring Pty Ltd, Australian Pacific (Holdings) Pty Ltd, and their subsidiaries and related entities which operate the APT, Travelmarvel, TravelGlo, Botanica World Discoveries, Captain’s Choice and OneTomorrow brands. APT is the controller responsible for your personal data (collectively referred to “we”, “us” or “our” in this Privacy Policy).


We comply with the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) as contained in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Along with other regional regulations like the GDPR, the APPs detail how personal information may be collected, used, disclosed, stored and destroyed, and how an individual may gain access to or make complaints about the personal information held about them.

There are different kinds of data, below are some examples:
• Identity Data includes first name, last name, date of birth and gender.
• Contact Data includes address, email address and telephone numbers.
• Financial Data includes bank account and payment card details.
• Technical Data includes IP address, your login data, and your browser type.
• Profile Data includes your username and password and survey responses.


We may collect anonymised details about your use of the websites for the purposes of aggregate statistics or reporting purposes. Aggregated data (your data combined with other people’s data) may come from your personal data but if it does not directly or indirectly reveal your identity, it is not considered personal data. For example, we may combine and analyse your use of the website to work out the number of users accessing a specific website feature.


Personal information is information or an opinion about an identified individual, or about an individual who is reasonably identifiable. We collect personal information from and about our prospective and current customers, as well as from and about travel agents, business partners and other travel suppliers.


Sensitive Information, a sub-set of personal information, includes information or an opinion about an individual’s racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, political association membership, religious beliefs or affiliations, philosophical beliefs, professional or trade association membership, trade union membership, sexual orientation or practices or criminal record, as well as health, genetic and biometric information. We collect sensitive information from and about our customers where such information is included in Government-issued identity documents (e.g. passport), and from health and mobility questionnaires.


Health Information is information or an opinion about an individual’s health or disability, the health services provided or to be provided to them, their expressed wishes for the provision of future health services, personal information collected to provide a health service, personal information collected in connection with organ and body-part donation, and predictive genetic information.


This policy details how APT manages personal information about you (including sensitive information and health information), whether you are a customer, a travel agent, an employee or another kind of travel supplier to our business.


In the course of offering our travel products and services, the collection of personal information is necessary and unavoidable. However, we aim to only collect personal information that is reasonable and fair in order to deliver the best possible travel products and services.


We take our obligations very seriously and have appointed a Privacy Officer for Australia, New Zealand and North America and a Data Protection Officer for Europe and the United Kingdom (together and separately (as applicable) the “DPO”) who are responsible for overseeing questions or concerns you may have about this Privacy Policy, including any requests to exercise your legal rights. The APT contact details are shown at the end of this policy.


It is important that the personal data we hold about you is accurate and current. Please keep us informed if your personal data changes during your relationship with us.

LEGAL RIGHTS UNDER THE GDPR

Under certain circumstances, the GDPR grants you certain rights under information protection laws in relation to your personal information. You have the right to:


1. Request access to your personal information (commonly known as a “data subject access request”). This enables you to receive a copy of the personal information we hold about you and to check that we are lawfully processing it.


2. Request correction of the personal information that we hold about you. This enables you to have any incomplete or inaccurate information we hold about you corrected, though we may need to verify the accuracy of the new information you provide to us.


3. Request erasure of your personal information. This enables you to ask us to delete or remove personal information where there is no good reason for us continuing to process it. You also have the right to ask us to delete or remove your personal information where you have successfully exercised your right to object to processing (see below), where we may have processed your information unlawfully or where we are required to erase your personal information to comply with local law. Note, however, that we may not always be able to comply with your request of erasure for specific legal reasons which will be notified to you, if applicable, at the time of your request.


4. Object to processing of your personal information where we are relying on a legitimate interest (or those of a third party) and there is something about your particular situation which makes you want to object to processing on this ground as you feel it impacts on your fundamental rights and freedoms. You also have the right to object where we are processing your personal information for direct marketing purposes. In some cases, we may demonstrate that we have compelling legitimate grounds to process your information which override your rights and freedoms.


5. Request restriction of processing of your personal information. This enables you to ask us to suspend the processing of your personal information in the following scenarios:

-if you want us to establish the information’s accuracy;
-where our use of the information is unlawful but you do not want us to erase it;
-where you need us to hold the information even if we no longer require it as you need it to establish, exercise or defend legal claims; or
-you have objected to our use of your information but we need to verify whether we have overriding legitimate grounds to use it.


6. Request the transfer of your personal information to you or to a third party. We will provide to you, or a third party you have chosen, your personal information in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format. Note that this right only applies to automated information which you initially provided consent for us to use or where we used the information to perform a contract with you.
7. Withdraw consent at any time where we are relying on consent to process your personal information. However, this will not affect the lawfulness of any processing carried out before you withdraw your consent. If you withdraw your consent, we may not be able to provide certain products or services to you. We will advise you if this is the case at the time you withdraw your consent.


If you wish to exercise any of the rights set out above, our contact details are shown at the end of this policy.

NO FEE USUALLY REQUIRED

Thin Green Line

Worldwide


Thin Green Line is a global not-for-profit organisation that exists to support park and wildlife rangers in their fight for conservation.

Rangers play a key role in safeguarding the natural, cultural, and historical values of the world’s protected areas against threats such as the illegal wildlife trade, invasive species, and, increasingly, the adverse impacts of climate change. Yet, the role they play as the first line of defence against these threats remains poorly recognised and inadequately resourced.


The Problem

Today we are facing increasing challenges around the Globe: climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and pandemics with a high human and economic impact. These and many other problems are closely linked to a deteriorating environment generated by our unsustainable production and consumption patterns which heavily depend on nature and its services.


The Solution

Protected areas are one the most effective tools for the conservation of biodiversity. However, no protected area is manageable without Park Rangers. Rangers working in protected and conserved areas are responsible for managing large tracts of the planet’s lands and waters. They are often underutilized, underrecognized and underequipped. Men and women rangers around the planet are key to securing and improving management of all protected areas.

$35 can provide an essential first aid kit.

$110 can provide a pair of sturdy waterproof walking boots.

$220 can provide a GPS unit to enable rangers to communicate and stay safe while working in remote areas in often challenging conditions.

Terry Fox Foundation

Canada


This story is simple and powerful. Terry Fox lost his leg to osteogenic sarcoma at age 18, underwent 16 months of treatment and found he could not ignore the suffering he witnessed in the cancer wards. Terry decided to run across Canada to raise money for cancer research in a Marathon of Hope. He wasn’t doing the run to become famous; he wanted to create change and fund a cure for all cancers.


The Problem

Terry died on June 28, 1981 at the age 22. This bold and courageous Canadian was gone, but his legacy was just beginning. To date, over $900 million has been raised for cancer research in Terry’s name through the annual Terry Fox Run, held across Canada and around the world. Nearly 2 in 5 people in Canada will develop cancer during their lifetime and about 1 out of 4 Canadians are expected to die from cancer.


The Solution

Terry’s personal experience and research led him to a simple conclusion – more money was needed for cancer research. We support bold, innovative cancer research across Canada that helps lead to better diagnosis, treatment options and quality of life for those facing cancer. We invest your donations in the very best scientists in laboratories, clinics, and hospitals around the country.


What difference will your money make?

$100 will accelerate cancer research

$200 is an investment in the future that ensures we can continue to make progress in the fight against cancer for future generations.

$500 can support the Canadian Tissue Repository Network (CTRNet)

Grizzly Bear Foundation

Canada


In 2014 home builder, philanthropist and art collector Michael Audain, O.C., O.B.C., was visited by a grizzly bear and her two cubs in a dream. Curious, Michael travelled to the Great Bear Rainforest, where he lived a similar personal experience. Inspired, Michael returned to Vancouver to establish the Grizzly Bear Foundation.


The Problem

Prior to the Grizzly Bear Foundation the majestic Grizzly Bear had no voice in our communities, governments, and in the public’s hearts and minds. Sparked by the fight to end the hunting of grizzly bears in British Columbia, Michael’s vision to ensure a safe and healthy future for grizzly bears all across North America continues to fuel the Grizzly Bear Foundation’s important work many years later.


The Solution

We believe coexistence with grizzly bears is possible. As an organization, we work with communities, governments, and industry to achieve this goal. We support human-bear coexistence through research, outreach, and education by working collaboratively with the BC Conservation Officer Service, the Ministry of Agriculture, First Nations, partner organizations, and local communities.


To foster coexistence, we host public workshops, social activities, presentations, and webinars and produce informational brochures, podcasts and videos to further non-lethal coexistence tools and techniques.


What difference will your money make?

$300 will support our advocacy and policy reform projects to secure long-term protection.

$500 will support Indigenous leadership in long-term grizzly bear conservation.

$1000 will help reduce human-bear conflict and promote coexistence.

Habitat for Humanity

New Zealand

Habitat for Humanity holds the fundamental belief that everyone deserves a decent place to live. Habitat for Humanity’s housing initiatives and advocacy efforts in Aotearoa New Zealand and the Pacific are all designed to build pathways that lead towards an adequate home, whatever that may mean for a person or family’s personal journey, culture or circumstance. From supplying curtains to facilitating home ownership, Habitat’s many pathways are formed on the pillars of education, adequacy and stability through safe shelter.

The Problem

The Pacific Islands face ever-increasing severe weather that affects homes and livelihoods, including an annual cyclone season. Often homes are damaged or destroyed by high tides, storms, or natural disasters while still recovering from the last severe event. Repairs and strengthening of homes can be limited by access to finances, specific skills, or materials in remote locations.

The Solution

Habitat for Humanity partners with communities in Samoa, Fiji and Tonga through community trainings. Shelter trainings are run by local organisations for local communities to make themselves and their homes more resilient. When the next weather event occurs, communities are better prepared with strengthened housing and the skills to recover quickly if needed. Local communities develop plumbing skills, home repair knowledge, and community action plans to make their homes better prepared for extreme weather and a changing environment.

Tanzania

In 1976, Kilimatembo school officially opened its doors to students in rural Tanzania. Since then, the school has been providing education to local children to pave the way for a brighter future. Kilimatembo emphasises the importance of conservation and environmental education; encouraging children to participate in numerous nature-based activities, including tree planting and caring for plants in the school’s garden.

The Problem

Remote and isolated, Kilimatembo is a two-hour drive from the nearest major city. This means that resources are often scarce. Without regular funding, supplies like school books, clean drinking water and even salary and accommodation for teachers cannot be sustained. Without these essential tools, opportunities for the children at Kilimatembo are considerably limited.

The Solution

Regular donations will assist the maintaining of Kilimatembo school so it can continue to provide children with the education they deserve. This means acquiring water tanks for clean drinking water, a school kitchen, an ICT room, teacher accommodation, as well as computers, books and games for the children to use.

Wunan Foundation

Australia

Wunan Foundation was established in 1997 to improve the lives of Aboriginal people in the East Kimberley and drive sustainable change for the future. ‘Wunan’, a traditional ritual of Aboriginal people from the region, encompasses the idea of sharing and caring. With this mindset, Wunan works to achieve equality and long-term socioeconomic change. Its key areas of focus are: education, employment, housing, leadership, welfare reform and health.

The Problem

A number of root causes has resulted in long-term disadvantage for Aboriginal people in the East Kimberley. They are more likely to experience higher rates of chronic disease, unemployment and incarceration. Lack of opportunity has led to difficulties with education, employment and housing, as well as poor healthcare and substance abuse. These issues need to be addressed at a fundamental level in order to pave the way to a social and economic culture of support and opportunity.

The Solution

Wunan believes in providing opportunity and supporting the abilities of Aboriginal communities. With the right support, the unfair disadvantage faced by many Aboriginal people can change. Wunan Foundation’s programs include re-engaging students in school and training, increasing home ownership, providing career support, and running a driver’s license training program. Their main objective is to shift the balance of Aboriginal people dependent on welfare from 80% to 20% over the next 20 years. You can play a key part in making this happen.

$150 provides a day’s Remote School Attendance transport service.

$320 gives a child a week’s worth of housing in a KEEP house.

Gondwana Rainforest Trust

Australia

Gondwana Rainforest Trust is dedicated to safeguarding the future of the world’s rainforests. Programs include land buy-back, tree-planting, and unique partnerships with Traditional Custodians to ensure the protection and restoration of our rainforests. The Daintree Lowland Rainforest is the oldest rainforest on Earth, having existed continuously for over 120 million years. It holds exceptionally high biodiversity and conservation value and is the largest continuous area of tropical rainforest remaining in Australia. In only the last forty years, the rainforest has been under threat by over-development.


The Problem 

The 1980s saw the Queensland Government approve a rural residential subdivision within the Daintree Lowland Rainforest. This removed the land from the protection of the rainforest’s World Heritage status, resulting in the construction of roads and houses which introduced weeds and traffic pollution to the area. Due to these factors, rare and endangered species living in the rainforest are under threat. 


The Solution

Gondwana Rainforest Trust are buying back land to remove any threat of future development. At the same time, they are ensuring their efforts support the Traditional Land Owners of the Kuku Yalanji people. By buying properties currently residing in the Daintree Lowland Rainforest, the protected Daintree National Park and Wet Tropics World Heritage Area will regain its lost land. With your help, they can return the Daintree Rainforest to its former glory.


What difference will your money make?

Blue Dragon Children's Foundation

Vietnam

Blue Dragon provides children in Vietnam with care, shelter, legal advocacy and long-term support to improve their lives. Thanks to their ongoing work, children suffering from rural poverty, disability, human trafficking, homelessness and HIV/AIDs are given hope for a better future. To date, Blue Dragon has saved almost 1000 people from trafficking and helped over 5,100 children return to school.

The Problem

Poverty is a cycle, and for those born into it, the reality is it’s often inescapable. More than 66% of Vietnam’s population live in rural areas where rice farming is the main industry, earning families as little as $1 – $2 a day. Children often have to quit school and move far from home to seek work, putting them at risk of homelessness, trafficking, exploitation, drug abuse and illness.

The Solution

By donating to Blue Dragon, you create a pathway for a brighter future. While children receive immediate care and rescue, long-term change is carried out on a systematic level, affecting law reform, policy development and training programs. With our help, Blue Dragon can continue their work, giving exceptional care to the children who need it most.

$20 gives a night of emergency shelter, with clothing and meals

$150 keeps a child in school for a year

$1,000 will fund the rescue mission that saves someone from human trafficking.

Médecins San Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders)


Médecins Sans Frontières / Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation delivering emergency medical aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, natural disasters, and exclusion from healthcare in over 70 countries worldwide. MSF medical teams act fast to save people’s lives. Everywhere they work, the circumstances are unique, but rapid and effective response to emergencies is at the core of their work.


The Problem

When a crisis like COVID-19 strikes, MSF doctors, nurses and midwives are on the frontline of the response. Supported by 50 years of experience responding to emergencies, MSF teams work to protect the most vulnerable — people whose lives are in danger, who are at risk of hunger and disease, people trapped in conflict zones where health systems have collapsed, people who are excluded from healthcare, or at risk of exploitation.


The Solution

MSF provide free medical care to people who need it. It doesn’t matter which country they are from, which religion they belong to, or what their political affiliations are. All that matters is they are human beings in need.


In a conflict situation, MSF don’t take sides, but go where people’s medical needs are greatest. In the ward of one Médecins Sans Frontières field hospital, you might find wounded civilians alongside injured soldiers from opposing sides. Hostilities and weapons must be left at the gate.


What difference will your money make?

$25.00 per month over a year could provide urgent ready to use therapeutic food to 690 malnourished children

$45.00 per month over a year could provide 1350 vital vaccines to combat a measles outbreak.

$75.00 per month over a year could supply a medical team with emergency health kits to treat 300 people in need.

Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS)

Australia

Delivering aeromedical and primary healthcare across rural Australia, the RFDS has been serving Australians for over 90 years. Reverend John Flynn, founder of RFDS, had a vision to bring a ‘mantle of safety’ to those living in the bush. His powerful legacy lives on with an impact so significant that Flynn was immortalised on the Australian $20 note in 1994.

The Problem

With land about 32 times the size of the UK, people living in the most remote areas of Australia are cut-off from standard emergency services. For those who live, work or travel in rural regions, medical assistance can be difficult to access and the long distances can mean the worst when faced with life-threatening illness or injury.

The Solution

With its very own fleet of aircraft, the RFDS is equipped to serve Australians living in hard-to-reach places. With your donations, vital equipment like ventilators and foetal heart monitors can be purchased, health programs can be implemented and aircraft can be replaced, keeping the RFDS flying strong. Together, we can support their continued effort and dedication, as they help over 1,000 people every day in rural Australia.

What difference will your money make?

$30 will ensure children in remote areas of Australia can be immunised.

$150 will provide pilots with noise-cancelling headsets.

$500 will put a heart monitor in an aircraft or emergency vehicle.

Antarctic Science Foundation

Antarctica

The Antarctic Science Foundation is a “for-impact” organisation that brings together all people who believe in the value and potential of Antarctica to provide the answers we need to sustain our way of life on this planet.

The Problem

Antarctica and the Southern Ocean are the global engine room of Earth’s climate, profoundly influencing weather systems through its oceans and atmosphere. For more than 50 million years, they have acted as shock absorbers, gathering heat and carbon in the ocean, while the white continent reflects heat and radiation back into space.

At twice the size of Australia, this wild, pristine continent is now humanity’s “canary in the coal mine” and the focus of considerable change. Our challenge is to shape our future by listening and discovering what we need to know in the present.

The Solution

When you support the Antarctic Science Foundation, you will be backing dedicated, tenacious researchers to be curious as they confront uncertainty in the most extreme conditions. You will support these scientists to ask the important questions to sustain our way of life through tangible outcomes in:

  • Climate prediction for all Australians, living in our cities and those who live on the land
  • Fire, flood and drought prediction and mitigation
  • Managing economic and sustainable fisheries
  • Carbon capture and abatement via nature’s systems
  • Increasing the health of our oceans
  • Improving global biodiversity
  • Protection of Antarctic wildlife 

What difference will your money make?

$28 provides spatial analysis of a penguin’s breeding habits.

$95 provides for seawater analysis to understand impact of climate change on plankton and krill.

$270 provides a data-analysis session, a vital input models of interaction to develop climate change mitigation strategies.

$480 provides a seal tracker which will assist mapping of the undersides of ice-shelves.

$980 provides a marine probe to assess changes in whale habitats.
